title: TestCase
description: One REST API test case, stored as test-suites/<suite_id>/v<version>/tests/<id>.json. requirement_ids and overrides_applied are the traceability core of the workbench: a case with no requirement link makes its suite incomplete, and a case that depended on an override rule must name the exact rule version it followed so an auditor never has to re-read agent reasoning transcripts. Loom-work does not execute these cases; the execution contract hands them to an external runner.

id.description: Case identity within its suite version.

name.description: Tester-facing description of what the case proves.

requirement_ids.description: Requirement ids this case exercises. An empty list is schema-valid but flags the containing suite as incomplete, so an agent cannot hide unlinked tests by omitting the field.

overrides_applied.description: Override rule versions this case followed instead of the literal spec, as "<rule_id>-v<version>". Empty means the case follows the spec as written.

scenario.description: Test intent, from the same closed set as an override rule's condition.scenario, so rules and cases can be matched mechanically.

request.description: The request definition handed to the executor.

path.description: Path relative to the target environment's base URL, e.g. "/orders/does-not-exist".

headers.description: Request headers. Never store credentials here; the executor config supplies auth.

expected.description: The outcome the executor must assert. Structural only: value-level diffing is out of scope for this phase.

empty_collection.description: True when the response body must be an empty collection, the shape the confirmed empty-list override requires.

body_fields.description: Response fields that must be present, as dotted paths, e.g. "data.0.id".

max_latency_ms.description: Optional per-case latency budget the executor reports against.

notes.description: Free-text assertion detail for a human reviewer.

suite.title: TestSuite
suite.description: test-suites/<suite_id>/v<version>/suite.json: the manifest of one immutable suite version. It also defines the interchange document for both agent generation output and external suite import, in which case the cases array is present inline instead of case_ids; the store splits the cases into tests/<id>.json on write and reassembles them on read.

origin.description: generated: produced by an agent through the adapter layer. imported: authored outside Loom-work and versioned identically.

cases.description: Present in an interchange document (generation output or import payload). Absent in the stored manifest, where cases live in tests/.

case_ids.description: Present in the stored manifest: the case files under tests/, in suite order.

incomplete.description: True when the suite must not be treated as ready: at least one case has no requirement link, or the override audit found a case that ignored an applicable rule without citing it. Suites are stored either way; the flag exists so the UI surfaces the problem instead of silently accepting it.

incomplete_reasons.description: One entry per reason the suite is incomplete, naming the offending case ids.

agent_definition.description: Agent definition version that generated the suite, as "<agent_name>-v<version>". Absent for imported suites.

requirement_versions.description: Requirement id to the version supplied as input, so a suite records exactly which requirement snapshots it was generated against.

override_rules.description: Override rule versions supplied as input, as "<rule_id>-v<version>". A rule can be an input without any case applying it.

spec_ref.description: OpenAPI/Swagger document the suite was generated from: a project document source name, a path, or a URL.

current.title: TestSuiteCurrent
current.description: test-suites/<suite_id>/current.json: which version is the default execution target. Older versions stay retrievable but are not executed by default.
